entry.label: paper:6.5
entry.title: A cutoff version of the Leibniz square
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
From \cite{LWX126}, Remark 6.5 and Theorem 2.12.\par
In the quotient-boundary square used for the Leibniz argument, let $x,y,z,w$ be the four specified infinite-page labels at a common stem and weight, with top, left and bottom extension lengths $m,r,l$. The four-edge theorem permits a cutoff $c$ with
\[
0<c\le r+l-m.
\]
Besides the three input extensions and no crossing on the top or left edge, it suffices to require that the bottom extension has no crossing hitting filtration at least $s+m+c$, and that the right edge has an extension of length $c-1$ from $y$ to zero with no crossing. Then the right edge has an extension of length $r+l-m$ from $y$ to $w$.

This is the extension-square generalization proposed in the remark. Reading its right edge as a specified classical Adams differential additionally requires the boundary and label comparisons for that square; the cutoff does not by itself supply them. At positive lambda level the
same four-edge statement must be instantiated at the actual quotient
and weight of the level square, including the right-edge zero extension.
At level zero it remains this cutoff specialization; no arbitrary-level
classical differential theorem is asserted solely by choosing $c$.

entry.label: paper:6.8
entry.title: A crossing obstructing a Leibniz conclusion
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
From \cite{LWX126}, Example 6.8 and Remarks 6.6, 6.9--6.10.\par
Let $f=2:S^0\to S^0$, normalized by $[h_0]$. At
\[
n=r=2,\quad m=1,\quad l=2,\quad e(f)=1,\quad s=1,\quad t=16,
\]
the input relations are
\[
d_2(h_4)=h_0h_3^2,\qquad
d_1^{f,E_2}(h_4)=h_0h_4,\qquad
d_2^{f,E_\infty}(h_0h_3^2)=0.
\]
The bottom relation has the essential crossing
\[
d_1^{f,E_\infty}(d_0)=h_0d_0.
\]
Consequently, omitting the bottom no-crossing hypothesis from the original Leibniz rule would give the incorrect conclusion $d_3(h_0h_4)=0$.

The same shorter extension also makes
\[
d_2^{f,E_\infty}(h_0h_3^2)=h_0d_0
\]
inessential. Applying a rule without the required crossing control to these two choices would give the conflicting outputs
\[
d_3(h_0h_4)=0,\qquad d_3(h_0h_4)=h_0d_0.
\]
The issue persists if one merely chooses a lift with maximally lambda-divisible image: the article gives two lifts of $h_0h_3^2$, one with $[h_0]$-image zero and another with image $[h_0d_0]$. The first is the maximal choice in the sense discussed there, yet it would yield the incorrect zero conclusion. A maximal-image choice is not a replacement for the crossing hypothesis.

entry.label: paper:6.19
entry.title: The nu-cofiber calculation of a finite extension
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
From \cite{LWX126}, Example 6.19.\par
Consider
\[
S^3\xrightarrow{\nu}S^0\xrightarrow{i}C\nu\xrightarrow{q}S^4,
\qquad (e(\nu),e(i),e(q))=(1,0,0).
\]
In Atiyah--Hirzebruch notation, $a[4]$ has top-cell image $a$ and $b[0]$ denotes the bottom-cell image of $b$. The input data are
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_0^{q,E_2}(h_0h_4^2[4])&=h_0h_4^2,\\
d_2(h_0h_4^2[4])&=h_0p[0],\\
d_0^{i,E_2}(h_0p)&=h_0p[0],
\end{aligned}
\]
where $h_0p[0]$ is a permanent cycle. The classical $d_2$ and the length-zero $q$-extension have no crossing in the sense used in the article. With
\[
n=2,\quad m=l=0,\quad n_1=1,\quad m_1=l_1=0,
\quad r=r'=2,
\]
the claimed output is that $h_0h_4^2\in E_2^{3,36}(S^3)$ survives to $E_3$ and
\[
d_2^{\nu,E_3}(h_0h_4^2)=h_0p,
\qquad h_0p\in E_2^{5,38}(S^0).
\]

entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

From \cite{LWX126}, Example 6.24.\par
For $f=\nu:S^3\to S^0$, the finite relation of Example~\ref{paper:6.19},

is asserted in the article to extend to

entry.label: paper:6.7
entry.title: A classical d-three obtained by the Leibniz argument
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
From \cite{LWX126}, Example 6.7.\par
For $f=\nu:S^3\to S^0$, consider
\[
\begin{gathered}
x=h_5\in E_2^{1,35}(S^3),\qquad
y=h_2h_5\in E_2^{2,36}(S^0),\\
x_\infty=h_0h_4^2\in Z_\infty^{3,36}(S^3),\qquad
y_\infty=h_0p\in Z_\infty^{5,38}(S^0).
\end{gathered}
\]
The article applies the classical input and the two extensions
\[
d_2(h_5)=h_0h_4^2,\qquad
d_1^{f,E_2}(h_5)=h_2h_5,\qquad
d_2^{f,E_\infty}(h_0h_4^2)=h_0p
\]
with their specified no-crossing conditions to obtain
\[
d_3(h_2h_5)=h_0p.
\]
Its parameters are $n=r=2$, $m=1$, $l=2$, $e(f)=1$, $s=1$ and $t=35$.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ml-ss-scope
entry.title: Mathematical rules used by the synthetic computation routines
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
A mathematical transcription of the synthetic routines of
\cite{LinProgram,LWXZenodo}, using the fixed source-code release and
retaining its source-level conditions.

The differential rule has the shape
\[
d_bx=u,\qquad x\longmapsto y,\qquad u\longmapsto v
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_{b+L-M}y=v,
\]
where $M$ and $L$ are the two image filtration shifts. Its intended
mathematical explanation is the quotient-boundary square of generalized
Leibniz, including the cutoff of Remark~\ref{paper:6.5}. Hidden images
are sought by the Mahowald pattern: take an $h$ preimage, use a
differential, and take a $g$ preimage, with length relation $r=n+l+m$.
Classical extensions and permanent-cycle outputs additionally concern
full representatives and the realization of Proposition~\ref{paper:5.14}.

This section first states the mathematical extension rules and derives
the indicated specializations of the level-indexed tools. It then
specifies the actual partial-data tests, without replacing them by
assumed true extensions. The final comparison distinguishes a proved
specialization of a mathematical rule from the pending implication
from the program's tests to that rule's hypotheses. The two operational
soundness assertions retain the latter pending implication.

The routines do not enumerate the complete sufficient-condition packages
of \ref{sem:ProofTools:cprime} or \ref{sem:ProofTools:ml-classical-nc}.
Their staircase labels encode cycle, boundary and differential information.
They are not the lambda levels of \ref{sem:ProofTools:ml-finite-core}.
The source-level transcription and its soundness assertions have no Lean
binding and introduce no admitted mathematical input. The full-lift
permanence result below binds its existing proved public theorem.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-leibniz-specialization
entry.title: The zero-input-level Leibniz rule with actual crossing conditions
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
A specialization of
\ref{sem:ProofTools:generalized-leibniz-at-level}, using the filtration
shifts of the differential routine in \cite{LinProgram}.

In the fixed Standard model let $f:X\to Y$, $e=e(f)$ and
$F:\Sigma^{0,e}\nu X\to\nu Y$ be its actual normalized map. Suppose
\[
2\le n\le b,\qquad e\le M\le n-2+e,\qquad L\ge e.
\]
Take the specified labels
\[
\begin{gathered}
x\in E_2^{s,t}(X),\qquad y\in E_2^{s+M,t+M}(Y),\\
u\in Z_\infty^{s+b,t+b-1}(X),\qquad
v\in Z_\infty^{s+b+L,t+b+L-1}(Y).
\end{gathered}
\]
Assume the actual equations
\[
d_bx=u,\qquad \mathcal E^f_{n-1,0}(M;x,y),\qquad
d_L^F(u)=\lambda^{L-e}v.
\]
Put $p=(t-s,t+e)$ and $A=\Sigma^{0,e}\nu X$. Require
\[
\bigl(NC(F_{n-1};p,s,M)\lor
 NC(\delta_{n-1}^A;p,s,b)\bigr)
\land NC(\Sigma^{1,-(n-1)}F;p,s+b,L).
\]
Then
\[
d_{b+L-M}(y)=v.
\]
An original page-extension input $d_M^{f,E_n}(x)=y$ supplies the
middle equation by \ref{sem:ProofTools:extension-level-zero}; the
crossing conditions in this corollary remain conditions on the actual
maps at the displayed weight.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-cutoff-square-specialization
entry.title: The cutoff Leibniz square at an arbitrary lambda level
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
A quotient-boundary specialization of the four-edge theorem
\ref{paper:2.12} and Remark~\ref{paper:6.5}.

Fix $F:A\to B$ with $A=\Sigma^{0,e}\nu X$, $B=\nu Y$. For
$n\ge2$ and a lambda level $k\ge0$ put $q=n+k-1$. Use the actual
commutative square
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
Q_qA&\xrightarrow{F_q}&Q_qB\\
\delta_q^A\downarrow&&\downarrow\delta_q^B\\
\Sigma^{1,-q}A&\xrightarrow{\Sigma^{1,-q}F}&\Sigma^{1,-q}B.
\end{array}
\]
Here $Q_qA=A/\lambda^q$. Fix a stem and weight $p=(a,w)$, and actual
infinite-page classes $\xi,\eta,\zeta,\omega$ in the four vertices,
at filtrations $s,s+M,s+b,s+b+L$, respectively; the remaining degree
coordinates are $(a+\mathrm{filtration},w)$.
Let $M,b,L\ge0$, $D=b+L-M$ and $1\le\kappa\le D$.
Assume
\[
d_M^{F_q}(\xi)=\eta,\qquad
d_b^{\delta_q^A}(\xi)=\zeta,\qquad
d_L^{\Sigma^{1,-q}F}(\zeta)=\omega.
\]
Require no crossing on the top or left equation. Require that the
bottom equation have no crossing hitting filtration at least
$s+M+\kappa$. Finally require the actual right-edge equation
\[
d_{\kappa-1}^{\delta_q^B}(\eta)=0
\]
with no crossing. Every crossing here is measured in the extension
spectral sequence of its actual edge, at the fixed stem and weight,
with its full shorter-image indeterminacy. Then
\[
d_D^{\delta_q^B}(\eta)=\omega.
\]
This is an extension-square conclusion. To read it as a specified
classical Adams differential, its labels must also have the required
boundary-comparison form. For example, use the classical labels,
degrees and range bounds of \ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-leibniz-specialization}.
If the actual comparisons give
\[
\begin{gathered}
\xi=\lambda^k x,\quad
\eta=\lambda^{k+M-e}y,\\
\zeta=\lambda^{b-n}u,\quad
\omega=\lambda^{b-n+L-e}v,
\end{gathered}
\]
at weight $t+e-k$, then the exponent identity
\[
D-q-1+(k+M-e)=b-n+L-e
\]
is precisely the arithmetic required for the right boundary to decode
as $d_Dy=v$. Those range bounds give $D\ge2$ and
$0\le k+M-e<q$. Actual qualified labels and comparisons remain
required; the exponent identity alone is not the decoding theorem.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-mahowald-specialization
entry.title: The finite Mahowald rule with both input levels zero
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
A specialization of the finite-layer revision
\ref{paper:6.12}, retaining the hidden-image pattern used in
\cite{LinProgram}.

Fix the same compatible normalized triangle and comparisons as in
\ref{paper:6.12}. Let
\[
\begin{gathered}
n_1=n-e_f\ge1,\quad m_1=m-e_g\ge0,\quad
k=l-e_h\ge0,\\
r=n+m+l,\qquad A=n_1+k,\quad B=m_1+1,\quad
r'=n_1+k+1.
\end{gathered}
\]
Thus $A+B=r$, $e_f+e_g+e_h=1$ and $r-k=n+m+e_h$.
Take the prescribed labels
\[
\begin{gathered}
\bar x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(Z),\quad
\bar y\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(Z),\\
x\in Z_{n_1}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X),\quad
y\in Z_{m_1+1}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y),
\end{gathered}
\]
with $d_r\bar x=\bar y$. For the actual finite maps and transported
labels of \ref{paper:6.12}, suppose
\[
d_l^{h_A}(\bar x)=\lambda^kx,\qquad
d_r^{\delta_{A,B}}(\bar x)=\lambda^{B-1}\bar y,\qquad
d_m^{g_B}(y)=\lambda^{B-1}\bar y.
\]
Require actual no-crossing on the $h_A$ equation or the
$\delta_{A,B}$ equation in the same weight. Their source class is
the same specified $\bar x$, and their common boundary target is
the same top-layer class, not just independently chosen labels.
Then there are the common actual representatives of
\ref{paper:6.12}, with
\[
\rho(c)=h_A(a),\qquad f_r(c)=-\lambda^Ab,
\]
and the conclusions
\[
x\in Z_{r-k},\qquad
d_n^{\widehat f_r}(\lambda^kx)=[\lambda^{r'-1}y].
\]
The source denominator is $B_{k+1}$ and the target denominator is
$B_{r'}$, with the shorter images of this same actual map also
retained. If $k=0$, this gives the ordinary level-zero page relation
in quotient $Q_r$, namely $\mathcal E^f_{r,0}(n;x,y)$, of effective
classical page $r+1$. If $k>0$, it retains the output level $k$;
the two zero input levels do not make its output level zero.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-partial-adams-data
entry.title: Partial Adams data and candidate subspaces
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
From the staircase and linear-algebra conventions of \cite{LinProgram}.

Fix the actual $E_2$ spaces $V_W^d=E_2^d(W)$ over $\mathbb F_2$,
where $d=(s,t)$, with their specified coordinates. Regard their finite
coordinate spaces as subspaces of the common space
$\mathbb F_2^{(\mathbb N)}$ of finitely supported coordinate vectors.
This convention permits the same raw vector to be assigned different
degrees; it does not supply a map between the corresponding $E_2$ spaces.
Every label, including
a zero vector, carries its assigned degree $d$; its filtration coordinate
below is $s(d)$, not an intrinsic filtration assigned to zero.
In every degree take
an ordered staircase basis $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ with nondecreasing integer
labels $\ell_i$. A row also carries a coordinate vector $\Delta_i$, or
the information that this vector is not yet determined. Put
\[
N=10000,\qquad R=1000,\qquad P=N-R,
\qquad D_W^d(<a)=\langle e_i:\ell_i<a\rangle.
\]
These integers encode the source conventions; $R$ is the permanent-page
sentinel, not a theorem identifying an arbitrary finite page with infinity.
A label $r<N/2$ records a boundary with a specified or undetermined
$d_r$ preimage. A label $N-r>P$ records a class reaching $E_r$ with its
$d_r$ specified or undetermined. The label $P$ records a permanent cycle.
Zero and an undetermined vector are distinct.

For $v\ne0$, let $\ell(v)$ be the largest label used in its staircase
basis expansion. Define $\Gamma(v)$ by summing the $\Delta_i$ only over
the terms in that largest-label block; it is undefined if any used
column of that block is undetermined. Put $\ell(0)=-1$ and
$\Gamma(0)=0$. Thus $\Gamma$ is a partially specified map on the
associated grades of the recorded flag with raw coordinate output.
On a boundary block of label $r$, its output is the coordinate vector
of a preimage in degree $d-(r,r-1)$, not an outgoing differential.

For a complete correct state, with $E_r=Z_{r-1}/B_{r-1}$, the finite
page conventions give, only in the encoded nonsentinel range $2\le r<R$,
\[
D(<r)=B_{r-1},\qquad D(<N-r)=Z_r.
\]
The correctly interpreted permanent and boundary blocks separately give
\[
D(<P)=B_\infty,\qquad D(<P+1)=Z_\infty.
\]
For partial data, $D$ denotes the recorded subspace itself; it must not
be replaced by a complete cycle or boundary space without a comparison.

Say that degree $d=(s,t)$ has an undetermined incoming possibility of
length at most $b$ if, for some $2\le a\le\min(b,s)$, degree
$d-(a,a-1)$ has a staircase row whose column is undetermined and whose
label is at least $N-a$. Define $U_W^d$ as follows. Remove the largest
terminal sequence of whole equal-label blocks such that every removed
label is at least $P+1$, every column is determined, and, for a block
of label $N-r$, its target degree $d+(r,r-1)$ has no undetermined
incoming possibility of length at most $r-1$. Then $U_W^d$ is the span
of the remaining initial basis segment. This is the candidate space
used by the image rule; it is not defined to be $Z_\infty$.

For each recorded subspace $C$, let $R_C$ denote its specified
Gaussian-elimination remainder map. For each matrix $A$, fix the
elimination selector $\sigma_A$ in the source's basis order. It is a
right inverse on $\operatorname{im}A$; its elimination formula is also
defined on inputs outside that image, without asserting
$A\sigma_A(v)=v$ there. All uses below retain the indicated degrees
and the specified coordinates.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-cutoff-data
entry.title: The recorded differential range and crossing bound
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
From the range queries of \cite{LinProgram}.

Use the data of \ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-partial-adams-data}. For a
coordinate vector $v$, define its recorded differential range
$\mathcal R(v)=(r_0,w_0)$ by
\[
\mathcal R(v)=
\begin{cases}
(R-1,0),&\ell(v)<N/2,\\
(N-\ell(v),\Gamma(v)),&\ell(v)\ge N/2\text{ and }\Gamma(v)
  \text{ is defined},\\
(N-\ell(v)-1,0),&\ell(v)\ge N/2\text{ and }\Gamma(v)
  \text{ is undefined}.
\end{cases}
\]
An undetermined $d_r$ therefore supplies only the preceding zero range,
not a claim that $d_r=0$. A boundary or zero vector uses the sentinel
zero range.

Let $\ell_{\max}(d)$ be the largest label in a nonempty degree. For
an integer $E$, define the recorded crossing bound
\[
\chi_E(d)=\min\left(
\{R\}\cup
\left\{j+N-\ell_{\max}(d+(j,j)):
\begin{array}{c}
1\le j\le E-2,\\
\ell_{\max}(d+(j,j))>N/2
\end{array}\right\}\right).
\]
Empty degree components contribute nothing. This uses the earliest
differential page not excluded by the recorded labels at a higher
filtration; it does not require a known nonzero crossing differential.
In particular, $\chi_E(d)\le b$ does not certify the existence of an
actual crossing. The degrees used in this formula have their given
$E_2$ coordinate spaces and declared zero spaces; bounds of the
computed tables are not mathematical hypotheses of the rule.

entry.title: Finite recursive image certificates
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
A branchwise mathematical transcription of the image tests in
\cite{LinProgram}.

Fix one cofiber triangle and its specified degree-shifted $E_2$ matrices
\[
H:V_Z\longrightarrow V_X,\qquad F:V_X\longrightarrow V_Y,
\qquad G:V_Y\longrightarrow V_Z.
\]
Write $\delta_F,\delta_G,\delta_H$ for their bidegree shifts and
$s(d),t(d)$ for the coordinates of a degree. Rotation of the triangle
specifies the matrices for recursive uses. All subspaces, selectors
and partial queries are those of
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-partial-adams-data}.

The relation
\[
\mathcal I_f(x;\ell,a,c)\rightsquigarrow(d_y,y)
\]
means that there is a finite derivation tree satisfying the following
clauses. The inputs are $x\in V_X^{d_x}$, its requested status $\ell$,
an ambiguity threshold $a$, and a crossing target threshold $c$.
The relation is defined by these algebraic clauses, not by the
existence of a true topological extension.

\textit{Ordinary-image clause.}
Let $y_0=F(x)$ and $d_0=d_x+\delta_F$. If
\[
y_0\ne0,\qquad \ell(y_0)\ge s(d_0)-a,
\]
there is the leaf conclusion $(d_y,y)=(d_0,y_0)$. The subsequent kernel
and crossing clauses do not apply to this leaf.

\textit{Hidden-image source clauses.}
Otherwise construct $z,u,d_z$ in one of the following ways.
If $F(x)=0$, put
\[
d_z=d_x-\delta_H,\qquad z=\sigma_H(x),\qquad u=\Gamma(z),
\]
and require $u$ to be defined and $\ell(z)>\ell$. Here $H$ is evaluated
on the staircase basis in its prescribed order. The assertion $H(z)=x$
is supplied by the actual matrix exactness
$\ker F=\operatorname{im}H$ when that comparison has been established;
it is not a separate image-membership test in this branch.

If $y_0=F(x)\ne0$ but $\ell(y_0)<s(d_0)-a$, require $w=\Gamma(y_0)$
to be defined, and put
\[
\begin{gathered}
d_w=d_0-(\ell(y_0),\ell(y_0)-1),\qquad
d_z=d_w+\delta_G,\\
z=G(w)\ne0,\qquad u=\Gamma(z)\text{ defined}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Require
\[
\ell(z)>\ell-(s(d_x)-s(d_z)),
\]
a recursive certificate
\[
\mathcal I_h(z;\ell(z),-1,0)\rightsquigarrow(d_x,x_1),
\]
and the exact recorded congruence
\[
x_1-x\in D_X^{d_x}(<\ell).
\]
For complete data and $\ell=N-b$, this is congruence modulo $Z_b$,
so it preserves the $d_b$ value, rather than specifying the same
$E_b$ class. For boundary status $\ell=b$, its denominator is instead
$B_{b-1}$.

\textit{Target equation and ambiguity clauses.}
For either hidden-image source, set
\[
q=N-\ell(z),\quad d_u=d_z+(q,q-1),\quad d_y=d_u-\delta_G,
\quad C=D_Z^{d_u}(<q),\quad A=R_C\circ G.
\]
Here the raw output $u=\Gamma(z)$ is reassigned to degree $d_u$.
A typed certificate requires its coordinate indices to be valid in
$V_Z^{d_u}$, as for every other degree assignment in these clauses.
For a boundary status, this is a different degree from the preimage
degree $d_z-(\ell(z),\ell(z)-1)$. Reusing the raw coordinates neither
defines a natural map between these degrees nor establishes $u=d_qz$;
the outgoing-differential interpretation has to be justified where used.
Require exactly one of the following according to the input status:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\ell\le P:
 &u\in A(U_Y^{d_y}),\qquad
   \ker(A|_{U_Y^{d_y}})\subseteq D_Y^{d_y}(<s(d_y)-a),\\[2pt]
\ell>P:
 &u\in\operatorname{im}A,\qquad
   s(d_y)\ge c\ \Longrightarrow\ \ker A=0.
\end{array}
\]
In the first case choose $y=\sigma_{A|_{U_Y^{d_y}}}(u)$; in the
second choose $y=\sigma_A(u)$. Thus the tested equation is
\[
R_C(G(y))=u.
\]
The right-hand side is not replaced by $R_C(u)$: the specified target
must already be a normal representative in this equation. In the
first case the selector uses the staircase basis of $U_Y^{d_y}$;
in the second it uses the original coordinate basis of the entire
$E_2$ space. For complete data the first kernel bound reads
$\ker(A|_{U_Y^{d_y}})\subseteq B_{s(d_y)-a-1}$.

\textit{Crossing clause.}
This clause is imposed only if $s(d_y)\ge c$. For each
\[
s(d_x)<s'<s(d_y)-s(\delta_F),\qquad
d'=(s',s'+t(d_x)-s(d_x)),
\]
and each staircase basis vector $e_i\in V_X^{d'}$ with $\ell_i\ge\ell$,
require either a child certificate
\[
\mathcal I_f(e_i;\ell_i,a,R)\rightsquigarrow(d'_y,y'),
\]
or the following immediate stopping condition:
\[
F(e_i)=0,\qquad z_i=\sigma_H(e_i),\qquad
\Gamma(z_i)\text{ defined},\qquad \ell(z_i)\le\ell_i.
\]
This exception concerns that candidate itself; a failure inherited
from one of its recursive calls is not an allowed stop.
For a child certificate whose target satisfies
$c\le s(d'_y)\le s(d_y)$, impose
\[
\begin{cases}
\text{no such child is allowed},&\ell>P,\\
y'=0\text{ or }y'\notin U_Y^{d'_y},&\ell\le P.
\end{cases}
\]
The first case also excludes a zero returned vector at a target degree
in that range. These are tests on the indicated basis vectors; the
definition does not silently quantify over all their linear combinations.
All recursive certificates are finite. No termination theorem or
topological soundness statement is built into this definition.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-adams-soundness
entry.title: Soundness assertion for the recorded Adams differential rule
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
The mathematical assertion used by the differential routine of
\cite{LinProgram}; its correctness under the following tested conditions
remains to be proved.

Fix actual spectra in a cofiber triangle, their specified normalized
maps and $E_2$ coordinates. Let the current partial Adams data correctly
record the already established cycles, boundaries, differential values
and permanent labels. All coordinates and partial queries below have
their specified degrees; no desired new differential is part of this
data-correctness assumption.

Suppose an input relation $d_bx=u$, with $2\le b<R$, is recorded with $u\ne0$ as a
coordinate vector. This does not impose nonvanishing of its class on
the page. Put
\[
c_0=\begin{cases}
0,&\chi_b(d_x)\le b,\\
R,&\chi_b(d_x)>b,
\end{cases}
\]
and suppose there is a finite certificate
\[
\mathcal I_f(x;N-b,-1,c_0)\rightsquigarrow(d_y,y).
\]
Let $M=s(d_y)-s(d_x)$, let $\mathcal R(y)=(r_0,w_0)$, and set
\[
\kappa=\min\left(
\chi_{M-s(\delta_F)+2}(d_y),\quad
r_0+\mathbf 1_{w_0=0}\right).
\]
Suppose also that
\[
\mathcal I_f(u;b,s(d_y),s(d_y)+\kappa)
 \rightsquigarrow(d_v,v),\qquad s(d_v)\ge s(d_y)+\kappa.
\]
Then, with $n=s(d_v)-s(d_y)$, the asserted mathematical conclusion includes
\[
n\ge2,\qquad d_v=d_y+(n,n-1),
\]
the cycle qualifications needed to define $[y]$ and $[v]$ on $E_n$,
and the relation
\[
d_n([y])=[v]
\]
in the actual Adams spectral sequence of $Y$. Equivalently, if
$s(d_v)=s(d_x)+b+L$, its length is $n=b+L-M$.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-classical-soundness
entry.title: Soundness assertion for classical extension and permanent-cycle outputs
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
The mathematical assertion used by the cofiber-extension routine of
\cite{LinProgram}; its correctness under the following tested conditions
remains to be proved.

Use actual spectra, maps and correct partial Adams data as in
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-adams-soundness}. Assume also the established
data invariant that the cofiber-extension table represents known
Adams permanent classes and their classical extension information.
Take a source $x$ in that table whose outgoing extension remains
undetermined. Its permanence is inherited from this table invariant,
not inferred from the image routine's status argument.

Suppose there is a finite certificate
\[
\mathcal I_f(x;P,-1,0)\rightsquigarrow(d_v,v),
\]
and put
\[
n=s(d_v)-s(d_x),\qquad n\ne s(\delta_F),\qquad
v_0=R_{D_Y^{d_v}(<P)}(v).
\]
The asserted mathematical output includes the length and degree conditions
\[
n\ge0,\qquad
d_v=d_x+\bigl(n,n+t(\delta_F)-s(\delta_F)\bigr),
\]
and the classical homotopy extension
\[
d_n^f\bigl(x+B_\infty^{d_x}(X)\bigr)
 =v_0+B_\infty^{d_v}(Y).
\]
For $v_0\ne0$ the routine additionally asserts $v_0\in Z_\infty$.
If $v_0=0$, a zero extension remains an allowed output. Nonzero
remainder modulo the currently recorded boundaries does not assert
that the final $E_\infty$ class is nonzero.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-level-implications
entry.title: What the level-indexed results imply for the program rules
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
A comparison of the preceding mathematical specializations with the
operational assertions of \cite{LinProgram}.

The established specializations and their outstanding uses are as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The arbitrary-level Leibniz theorem implies
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-leibniz-specialization} by setting its lambda
level to zero. Its three equations, permanent-label qualifications
and actual no-crossing conditions are retained. The cutoff square
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-cutoff-square-specialization} follows instead
from the four-edge theorem at every quotient and weight; it retains
the crossing-free right-edge zero extension. A recorded zero range
for $y$ and the number $\kappa$ do not, without a comparison, supply
that extension or its no-crossing condition. The page used in the
first finite image relation must also satisfy the tool's length bounds.

\item The double-input-level Mahowald theorem implies
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-mahowald-specialization} by setting $i=j=0$.
This is a genuine generalization with respect to the two input
levels, with the same actual crossing and representative conditions.
The output still has level $k=l-e_h$. A zero-output-level assertion
requires $k=0$ or a proved division that preserves the prescribed
source and target. The allowed kernel and recursive congruence tests
in \ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-image-certificate} have not yet supplied
these actual representative and crossing hypotheses.

\item For classical-extension and permanent-cycle outputs, the finite
Mahowald conclusion must be followed by a target-preserving full
lift. The exact obstruction criterion is
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ml-representative-family-lift}. Once a full target
with the prescribed finite detector has been constructed,
\ref{sem:ProofTools:ss-full-lift-permanence} proves the original target
label permanent. Realization of a single full source and its actual
image then uses Proposition~\ref{paper:5.14}. The source's permanence
or the permanent-mode argument alone does not construct this lift.
\end{enumerate}

In logical terms, if $H_{\mathrm{GL}}(k)$ denotes the complete hypotheses
of the level-indexed Leibniz theorem and $Q_{\mathrm{GL}}$ its conclusion,
the proved implication gives
\[
\bigl[\,\forall k\ge0,\ H_{\mathrm{GL}}(k)\Longrightarrow
 Q_{\mathrm{GL}}\,\bigr]
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl[\,H_{\mathrm{GL}}(0)\Longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{GL}}\,\bigr].
\]
The additional implication from the actual program conditions to
$H_{\mathrm{GL}}(0)$, or to the appropriate cutoff hypotheses, is a
separate mathematical assertion. The same distinction applies to
the Mahowald specialization and its retained output layer. None of
these implications uses the two operational soundness assertions
as premises.

entry.label: sem:ProofTools:ss-soundness-boundary
entry.title: Remaining comparisons for the computation rules
entry.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
entry.body:
The source transcription separates several mathematical comparisons
that have not been completed by writing the preceding conditions.
First, the recorded matrices, flag subspaces, selectors and normal
representatives must be identified with the actual normalized triangle
and the indicated cycle and boundary information. This includes the
use of $\ker F=\operatorname{im}H$ when selecting an $H$ preimage and
the distinction between the two meanings of $\Gamma$.

Second, the recursive congruences and the allowed target kernels must
be transported into the appropriate representative relations. A
successful image certificate is not, by definition, a fine
$(f,E_\infty)$-extension with its original target label. Third, the
tests on basis vectors, their label restrictions and their sole
stopping exception must be related to all the actual ambiguities
required by the square or Mahowald argument. Finally, classical and
permanent-cycle outputs require the full lifting and realization
comparison described above.

The surjectivity and (NC1)--(NC2) theorems provide other sufficient
conditions for a finite composition. Applying either to the program
requires a proof connecting the particular certificate conditions to
its hypotheses; no such implication follows merely from the presence
of image and kernel computations. These unresolved comparisons neither
establish a counterexample to the program nor certify its correctness.
